title: Senior's toolkit: server-side requests and parsers
summary: Out-of-band testing with a listener you control, IMDSv2 enforcement, SocketsHttpHandler's ConnectCallback, safe XmlReaderSettings, and the analyzers that flag dangerous deserializers.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: server-side requests and parsers
steps.body: SSRF, XXE and deserialization bugs are often blind: nothing comes back in the response. Testers prove them out of band, and developers shut them with a few platform and framework settings.

toolkit.cmd: a listener you control (Burp Collaborator, interactsh, python3 -m http.server)
toolkit.what: Prove a blind SSRF or XXE: point the feature at a host you control and watch for the server's request. In the lab, `listen` on attacker does this. Only use public callback services with permission: they see the traffic too.
flags: a simple listener on a test host

toolkit.what: Enforce IMDSv2 on an instance: metadata needs a session token from a PUT, which a GET-only SSRF cannot send. Set the hop limit to 1 so containers on the host cannot reach it either.
flags: the token cannot travel past the instance
no metadata at all, if nothing needs it

toolkit.what: The .NET hook for outbound requests to user-chosen URLs: resolve the host yourself, refuse private and link-local addresses, connect to the address you checked (no DNS rebinding), and follow no redirects.
toolkit.example:
builder.Services.AddHttpClient("webhooks", c => c.Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(3))
    .ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(() => new SocketsHttpHandler { AllowAutoRedirect = false, ConnectCallback = SafeConnect });

toolkit.cmd: new XmlReaderSettings { DtdProcessing = DtdProcessing.Prohibit, XmlResolver = null }
toolkit.what: The safe XML parser settings, written out so a reviewer sees them. Pass them to XmlReader.Create, then load XDocument or XmlDocument from that reader.
toolkit.example:
using var r = XmlReader.Create(stream, new XmlReaderSettings { DtdProcessing = DtdProcessing.Prohibit, XmlResolver = null });
var doc = XDocument.Load(r);

toolkit.what: Analyzer rules for dangerous deserializers: SYSLIB0011 flags BinaryFormatter; CA2300 to CA2330 flag BinaryFormatter, LosFormatter, NetDataContractSerializer, and Json.NET's TypeNameHandling without a binder. Make them errors.
toolkit.example:
[*.cs]
dotnet_diagnostic.CA2326.severity = error
dotnet_diagnostic.CA2327.severity = error
dotnet_diagnostic.SYSLIB0011.severity = error

steps.prompt: Match each setting to the attack it stops.
pairs: a GET-only SSRF stealing cloud credentials
an allowed host redirecting to an internal one
input that names its own .NET type

steps.prompt: The webhook feature lets customers enter any URL, so no host allow-list is possible. Which combination is right?
options: https only, an IP check on the resolved address at connect time, no redirects, a short timeout and a size cap, ideally through an egress proxy
A regex that rejects URLs containing '169.254'
Resolve the host once when the webhook is saved and trust it afterwards
steps.explain: A regex misses the other spellings, and a check at save time is defeated by changing DNS later. The connect-time check sees the address actually used.
